### GRI 302 Energy  
Amazon reported 131,000 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of carbon-free energy production annually in 2025 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_22]. Carbon-free energy includes electricity from wind, solar, nuclear, hydroelectric, and geothermal sources, as well as site energy contracts and green tariffs that add new renewable projects to the grid [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_14]. AWS aims to procure renewable electricity in the same grids where it consumes electricity; when not feasible, it may procure renewable energy attributes in other locations [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_113]. In 2025, Amazon’s emissions from purchased electricity (Scope 2) totaled 3.74 million metric tons of CO₂e (MMT CO₂e), representing a 34% increase from 2024 and 5% of its total carbon footprint [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_19][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_112]. This growth was driven by electricity use in data centers, electrification of the delivery network, and building electrification [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_19]. Amazon’s global data center portfolio achieved a Water Use Effectiveness (WUE) of 0.12 liters per kilowatt-hour (L/kWh) in 2025—a 20% improvement from 2024 and 52% since 2021—reflecting enhanced energy-water efficiency linkages [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_35].

### GRI 303 Water  
Amazon achieved 75% progress toward its goal of becoming water positive—returning more water to communities than it uses—across global direct data center operations by 2030 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33]. In 2025, Amazon’s global leased, owned, and shared data centers withdrew 9.4 billion liters of water [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33]. Of this, 48% occurred in low water stress regions and 22% in high or extremely high water stress regions, per WRI’s Aqueduct Water Risk Atlas [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_34]. Amazon measured progress using its Water Positive Methodology, which calculates the ratio of reused water plus replenishment volume to total water withdrawal minus water from sustainable sources, multiplied by 100% [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_16]. By end-2025, Amazon had invested in 45 water replenishment projects globally, returning 9.4 billion liters of water to communities and contracting for over 18 billion liters of annual replenishment volume in future years [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_37]. In India—where Amazon achieved 120% water positivity in 2025, two years ahead of its 2027 target—on-site sewage treatment plants at 28 buildings provided an estimated 298 million liters of recycled water annually, and rainwater harvesting pits collected ~178 million liters for groundwater recharge [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_37].

### GRI 305 Emissions  
Amazon’s total carbon footprint (Scopes 1, 2, and 3) was 80.85 MMT CO₂e in 2025, up 16% from 69.55 MMT CO₂e in 2024 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_113][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_5]. Scope 1 emissions were 15.37 MMT CO₂e, Scope 2 emissions were 3.74 MMT CO₂e, and Scope 3 emissions were 61.74 MMT CO₂e [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_112]. Environmental Attribute Certificates (EACs) delivered a net reduction of 199.4 thousand metric tons of CO₂e (K MTCO₂e) across Scopes 1, 3.1, 3.3, and 3.4—including 41.2 K MTCO₂e reduction in Scope 1 via Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) and Renewable Diesel certificates [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_15][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_113]. Carbon intensity—measured as grams of CO₂e per dollar of revenue—was 112.8 gCO₂e/$Revenue in 2025 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_112][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_5]. Amazon’s Climate Pledge commits to net-zero carbon emissions across global operations by 2040 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_10].

### GRI 306 Waste  
In 2025, Amazon diverted 84% of its operational waste from landfill and incineration without energy recovery—including 82% through recycling or composting and 2% through incineration with energy recovery [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_47]. Waste per shipped unit decreased by 5% compared to 2024 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_47][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_41]. Cardboard and wood constituted 64% of Amazon’s operational waste footprint, with nearly 100% recycled [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_47]. Amazon reused or donated 343,000 assets and materials in 2025 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_45], avoided over one million hard drive purchases since 2023 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_41], and prevented 225,000 metric tons of CO₂e through reuse and resale of data center hardware since 2020 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_45].

### TCFD Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics & Targets  
Amazon’s climate strategy is anchored in The Climate Pledge and structured around five pillars: reducing supply chain emissions, decarbonizing direct operations, addressing Scope 2 emissions, scaling carbon neutralization, and driving collective action [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_10]. Risk management integrates AI tools to identify high-risk suppliers and prioritize audits [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_10][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_13]. Key metrics include carbon intensity (gCO₂e/$Revenue), water use effectiveness (L/kWh), and waste diversion rate (%), with targets including net-zero by 2040, water positivity in data centers by 2030, and 100,000 electric delivery vans by 2030 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_5][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33].

The context does not specify whether Amazon reports location-based versus market-based Scope 2 emissions separately, nor does it disclose absolute Scope 3 subcategory totals beyond those listed in the 2019–2025 carbon footprint table (e.g., full breakdowns for all Scope 3 categories through 2025). In 2025, Amazon’s emissions from purchased electricity (Scope 2) totaled 3.74 million metric tons of CO₂e (MMT CO₂e), representing a 34% increase from 2024 and 5% of its total carbon footprint [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_19][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_112]. This growth was driven by electricity use in data centers, electrification of the delivery network, and building electrification [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_19]. Amazon’s global data center portfolio achieved a Water Use Effectiveness (WUE) of 0.12 liters per kilowatt-hour (L/kWh) in 2025—a 20% improvement from 2024 and 52% since 2021—reflecting enhanced energy-water efficiency linkages [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_35].

### GRI 303 Water  
Amazon achieved 75% progress toward its goal of becoming water positive—returning more water to communities than it uses—across global direct data center operations by 2030 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33]. In 2025, Amazon’s global leased, owned, and shared data centers withdrew 9.4 billion liters of water [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33]. Of this, 48% occurred in low water stress regions and 22% in high or extremely high water stress regions, per WRI’s Aqueduct Water Risk Atlas [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_34]. Amazon measured progress using its Water Positive Methodology, which calculates the ratio of reused water plus replenishment volume to total water withdrawal minus water from sustainable sources, multiplied by 100% [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_16]. By end-2025, Amazon had invested in 45 water replenishment projects globally, returning 9.4 billion liters of water to communities and contracting for over 18 billion liters of annual replenishment volume in future years [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_37]. In India—where Amazon achieved 120% water positivity in 2025, two years ahead of its 2027 target—on-site sewage treatment plants at 28 buildings provided an estimated 298 million liters of recycled water annually, and rainwater harvesting pits collected ~178 million liters for groundwater recharge [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_37].

### GRI 305 Emissions  
Amazon’s total carbon footprint (Scopes 1, 2, and 3) was 80.85 MMT CO₂e in 2025, up 16% from 69.55 MMT CO₂e in 2024 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_113][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_5]. Scope 1 emissions were 15.37 MMT CO₂e, Scope 2 emissions were 3.74 MMT CO₂e, and Scope 3 emissions were 61.74 MMT CO₂e [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_112]. Environmental Attribute Certificates (EACs) delivered a net reduction of 199.4 thousand metric tons of CO₂e (K MTCO₂e) across Scopes 1, 3.1, 3.3, and 3.4—including 41.2 K MTCO₂e reduction in Scope 1 via Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) and Renewable Diesel certificates [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_15][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_113]. Carbon intensity—measured as grams of CO₂e per dollar of revenue—was 112.8 gCO₂e/$Revenue in 2025 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_112][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_5]. Amazon’s Climate Pledge commits to net-zero carbon emissions across global operations by 2040 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_10].

### GRI 306 Waste  
In 2025, Amazon diverted 84% of its operational waste from landfill and incineration without energy recovery—including 82% through recycling or composting and 2% through incineration with energy recovery [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_47]. Waste per shipped unit decreased by 5% compared to 2024 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_47][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_41]. Cardboard and wood constituted 64% of Amazon’s operational waste footprint, with nearly 100% recycled [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_47]. Amazon reused or donated 343,000 assets and materials in 2025 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_45], avoided over one million hard drive purchases since 2023 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_41], and prevented 225,000 metric tons of CO₂e through reuse and resale of data center hardware since 2020 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_45].

### TCFD Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics & Targets  
Amazon’s climate strategy is anchored in The Climate Pledge and structured around five pillars: reducing supply chain emissions, decarbonizing direct operations, addressing Scope 2 emissions, scaling carbon neutralization, and driving collective action [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_10]. Risk management integrates AI tools to identify high-risk suppliers and prioritize audits [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_10][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_13]. Key metrics include carbon intensity (gCO₂e/$Revenue), water use effectiveness (L/kWh), and waste diversion rate (%), with targets including net-zero by 2040, water positivity in data centers by 2030, and 100,000 electric delivery vans by 2030 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_5][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33].

The context does not specify whether Amazon reports location-based versus market-based Scope 2 emissions separately, nor does it disclose absolute Scope 3 subcategory totals beyond those listed in the 2019–2025 carbon footprint table (e.g., full breakdowns for all Scope 3 categories through 2025). ### GRI 403 Occupational Health & Safety  
Amazon’s global operations safety performance showed consistent year-over-year improvement in 2025. The company reported a 14% year-over-year reduction in its Global Recordable Incident Rate (RIR), which measures work-related injuries requiring more than basic first-aid treatment, and a 14% year-over-year reduction in its Global Lost Time Incident Rate (LTIR), which measures injuries resulting in time away from work [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_76]. Over the past six years, Amazon improved its global RIR by 43% and its global LTIR by 70% [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_76][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_78]. In the U.S., under the General Warehousing and Storage industry classification, the RIR improved 16% year over year and 39% over six years; the LTIR was flat year over year but improved 79% over six years [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_76]. Under the Courier and Express Delivery Services classification, the RIR improved 19% year over year and 59% over six years, while the LTIR improved 28% year over year and 81% over six years [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_76]. Amazon conducted 10.4 million safety inspections globally in 2025—a 33% increase from 2024—to validate engineering controls and inform iterative improvements [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_77]. These efforts are supported by over 11,000 dedicated safety professionals worldwide [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_76].

### GRI 404 Training  
Amazon invested over $2.5 billion in safety efforts since 2019, including training programs grounded in prevention-through-design principles [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_78]. For employee development, Amazon launched the U.S. Mechatronics and Robotics Apprenticeship—a paid, Department of Labor–registered program combining classroom learning with on-the-job training—whose graduates earned on average $10,000 more annually than typical entry-level fulfillment-center wages, with 100% employment placement in 2025 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_70]. In 2025, 599,000 U.S. employees participated in upskilling programs since the 2019 Upskilling Pledge launch [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_69]. Additionally, over 16,400 U.S. employees completed English-language proficiency programs in 2025 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_69]. Amazon also delivered 52 new e-learning resources and updated 90 existing modules for human rights–related training, including a three-day immersive program for employees in human rights roles [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_63]. For suppliers, Amazon deployed online trainings for 1,600 suppliers on Supply Chain Standards and provided access to 90 third-party online trainings across 12 human rights topics [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_84].

### GRI 405 Diversity  
Amazon’s 2025 pay equity review found women globally earned 100.0% of what men earned in comparable jobs, and women in the U.S. earned 99.9 cents per dollar earned by men in comparable roles [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_71][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_70]. Racial and ethnic minorities in the U.S. earned 99.0 cents per dollar earned by white employees in comparable jobs [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_71][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_70]. The company expanded inclusive programming through “Together at Amazon,” reaching over 647,000 corporate and operations employees in 2025, including participation across 2,300 Employee-Led Groups (ELGs) spanning multiple countries and regions [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_75]. Amazon also advanced military inclusion via the Duty to Data Center program, placing veterans and military spouses into AWS Data Center Engineering roles, and introduced a Military Spouse Deployment Benefit [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_75].

### GRI 414 Supplier Social Assessment  
Amazon requires suppliers to comply with its Supply Chain Standards, available in 23 languages, and mandates that suppliers hold their own subcontractors and labor agents to applicable laws and these standards [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_84][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_83]. In 2025, Amazon hosted 29 in-person human rights workshops across 13 countries, engaging 650 participants from 480 suppliers; 60% of suppliers attending workshops between 2023 and 2025 reduced high-risk findings [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_84]. ### TCFD Strategy (social impacts of climate transition)  
Amazon aims to integrate human rights due diligence into its decarbonization efforts to identify how its shift to a green economy affects communities in its value chain [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_66]. ### GRI 302 Energy  
Amazon reported 131,000 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of carbon-free energy *procurement* annually in 2025 — defined as electricity from wind, solar, nuclear, hydroelectric, and geothermal sources, plus site energy contracts and green tariffs that add new renewable projects to the grid [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_22][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_14]. This includes 375 utility-scale projects (264 solar, 109 wind, two nuclear) and 337 rooftop solar installations across fulfillment centers and stores [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_22]. AWS aims to procure renewable electricity in the same grids where it consumes electricity; when infeasible, it may procure renewable energy attributes elsewhere [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_113]. Emissions from purchased electricity (Scope 2) totaled 3.74 million metric tons of CO₂e (MMT CO₂e) in 2025, up 34% from 2.80 MMT CO₂e in 2024 — driven by data center expansion, delivery network electrification, and building electrification [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_112][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_19]. Amazon’s global data center portfolio achieved a Water Use Effectiveness (WUE) of 0.12 liters per kilowatt-hour (L/kWh) in 2025 — a 20% improvement from 0.15 L/kWh in 2024 and 52% from 0.25 L/kWh in 2021 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_35].

### GRI 303 Water  
Amazon achieved 75% progress toward its goal of becoming water positive — returning more water to communities than it uses — across global direct data center operations by 2030 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33]. In 2025, its global leased, owned, and shared data centers withdrew 9.4 billion liters of water [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33]. Of this, 48% occurred in low water stress regions and 22% in high or extremely high water stress regions, per WRI’s Aqueduct Water Risk Atlas baseline [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_34]. Progress is measured using the Water Positive Methodology: (reused water + replenishment volume) ÷ (total withdrawal − water from sustainable sources) × 100% [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_16]. By end-2025, Amazon had invested in 45 water replenishment projects globally, returning 9.4 billion liters to communities and contracting for over 18 billion liters of annual replenishment volume in future years [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_37]. In India — where Amazon achieved 120% water positivity in 2025, two years ahead of its 2027 target — on-site sewage treatment plants at 28 buildings provided an estimated 298 million liters of recycled water annually [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_37].

### GRI 305 Emissions  
Amazon’s total carbon footprint (Scopes 1, 2, and 3) was 80.85 million metric tons of CO₂e (MMT CO₂e) in 2025, up 16% from 69.55 MMT CO₂e in 2024 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_113][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_5]. Scope 1 emissions were 15.37 MMT CO₂e, Scope 2 were 3.74 MMT CO₂e, and Scope 3 were 61.74 MMT CO₂e [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_112]. Environmental Attribute Certificates (EACs) delivered a net reduction of 199.4 thousand metric tons of CO₂e (K MTCO₂e) across Scopes 1, 3.1, 3.3, and 3.4 — including 41.2 K MTCO₂e reduction in Scope 1 via Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) and Renewable Diesel certificates [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_15][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_113]. Carbon intensity was 112.8 gCO₂e/$Revenue in 2025 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_112][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_5]. The Climate Pledge commits Amazon to net-zero carbon emissions across global operations by 2040 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_10], but the context does not specify the baseline year or disclose any SBTi-aligned interim targets.

### GRI 306 Waste  
In 2025, Amazon diverted 84% of its operational waste from landfill and incineration without energy recovery — including 82% through recycling or composting and 2% through incineration with energy recovery [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_47]. Waste per shipped unit decreased by 5% compared to 2024 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_47][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_41]. Cardboard and wood constituted 64% of Amazon’s operational waste footprint, with nearly 100% recycled [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_47]. ### GRI 302 Energy  
Amazon reported 131,000 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of carbon-free energy production annually in 2025 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_22]. Carbon-free energy includes electricity from wind, solar, nuclear, hydroelectric, and geothermal sources, as well as site energy contracts and green tariffs that add new renewable projects to the grid [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_14]. AWS aims to procure renewable electricity in the same grids where it consumes electricity; when not feasible, it may procure renewable energy attributes in other locations [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_113]. In 2025, Amazon’s emissions from purchased electricity (Scope 2) totaled 3.74 million metric tons of CO₂e (MMT CO₂e), representing a 34% increase from 2024 and 5% of its total carbon footprint [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_19][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_112]. This growth was driven by electricity use in data centers, electrification of the delivery network, and building electrification [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_19]. Amazon’s global data center portfolio achieved a Water Use Effectiveness (WUE) of 0.12 liters per kilowatt-hour (L/kWh) in 2025—a 20% improvement from 2024 and 52% since 2021—reflecting enhanced energy-water efficiency linkages [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_35].

### GRI 303 Water  
Amazon achieved 75% progress toward its goal of becoming water positive—returning more water to communities than it uses—across global direct data center operations by 2030 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33]. In 2025, Amazon’s global leased, owned, and shared data centers withdrew 9.4 billion liters of water [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33]. Of this, 48% occurred in low water stress regions and 22% in high or extremely high water stress regions, per WRI’s Aqueduct Water Risk Atlas [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_34]. Amazon measured progress using its Water Positive Methodology, which calculates the ratio of reused water plus replenishment volume to total water withdrawal minus water from sustainable sources, multiplied by 100% [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_16]. By end-2025, Amazon had invested in 45 water replenishment projects globally, returning 9.4 billion liters of water to communities and contracting for over 18 billion liters of annual replenishment volume in future years [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_37]. In India—where Amazon achieved 120% water positivity in 2025, two years ahead of its 2027 target—on-site sewage treatment plants at 28 buildings provided an estimated 298 million liters of recycled water annually, and rainwater harvesting pits collected ~178 million liters for groundwater recharge [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_37].

### GRI 305 Emissions  
Amazon’s total carbon footprint (Scopes 1, 2, and 3) was 80.85 MMT CO₂e in 2025, up 16% from 69.55 MMT CO₂e in 2024 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_113][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_5]. Scope 1 emissions were 15.37 MMT CO₂e, Scope 2 emissions were 3.74 MMT CO₂e, and Scope 3 emissions were 61.74 MMT CO₂e [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_112]. Environmental Attribute Certificates (EACs) delivered a net reduction of 199.4 thousand metric tons of CO₂e (K MTCO₂e) across Scopes 1, 3.1, 3.3, and 3.4—including 41.2 K MTCO₂e reduction in Scope 1 via Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) and Renewable Diesel certificates [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_15][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_113]. Carbon intensity—measured as grams of CO₂e per dollar of revenue—was 112.8 gCO₂e/$Revenue in 2025 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_112][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_5]. Amazon’s Climate Pledge commits to net-zero carbon emissions across global operations by 2040 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_10].

### GRI 306 Waste  
In 2025, Amazon diverted 84% of its operational waste from landfill and incineration without energy recovery—including 82% through recycling or composting and 2% through incineration with energy recovery [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_47]. Waste per shipped unit decreased by 5% compared to 2024 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_47][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_41]. Cardboard and wood constituted 64% of Amazon’s operational waste footprint, with nearly 100% recycled [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_47]. Amazon reused or donated 343,000 assets and materials in 2025 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_45], avoided over one million hard drive purchases since 2023 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_41], and prevented 225,000 metric tons of CO₂e through reuse and resale of data center hardware since 2020 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_45].

### TCFD Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics & Targets  
Amazon’s climate strategy is anchored in The Climate Pledge and structured around five pillars: reducing supply chain emissions, decarbonizing direct operations, addressing Scope 2 emissions, scaling carbon neutralization, and driving collective action [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_10]. Risk management integrates AI tools to identify high-risk suppliers and prioritize audits [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_10][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_13]. Key metrics include carbon intensity (gCO₂e/$Revenue), water use effectiveness (L/kWh), and waste diversion rate (%), with targets including net-zero by 2040, water positivity in data centers by 2030, and 100,000 electric delivery vans by 2030 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_5][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33].

### Not covered in source material  
The context does not specify whether Amazon reports location-based versus market-based Scope 2 emissions separately, nor does it disclose absolute Scope 3 subcategory totals beyond those listed in the 2019–2025 carbon footprint table (e.g., full breakdowns for all Scope 3 categories through 2025). It also lacks explicit disclosure on methane or other short-lived climate pollutant inventories outside of super pollutant abatement initiatives, and no quantitative data is provided on waste generation volumes (e.g., total tons of waste generated) — only diversion rates and intensity metrics.

### GRI 403 Occupational Health & Safety  
Amazon’s global operations safety performance demonstrated year-over-year improvement in 2025, with a 14% reduction in the Global Recordable Incident Rate (RIR) — defined as work-related injuries requiring more than basic first-aid treatment — and a 14% reduction in the Global Lost Time Incident Rate (LTIR) — defined as injuries resulting in time away from work [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_76][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_78]. Over six years, the global RIR improved by 43% and the global LTIR by 70% [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_76][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_78]. ### Board Oversight and Committee Structure  
Amazon’s Board of Directors is responsible for the control and direction of the company and represents shareholders with the primary purpose of building long-term shareholder value [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_101]. In 2025, the Board held six in-person meetings and participated in regularly scheduled teleconference discussions [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_101]. Risk oversight is delegated to four standing committees: the Audit Committee (six meetings), Leadership Development and Compensation Committee (five meetings), Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee (four meetings), and Security Committee (two meetings) [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_102]. The Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee oversees risks related to sustainability, environmental and corporate social responsibility practices, operations and supply chain, and responsible AI development and AI governance [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_102][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_103][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104]. The Chief Sustainability Officer provides regular updates to this committee on sustainability performance and human rights matters [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_103][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104].

### Anti-Corruption Governance and Controls  
Amazon’s Business Conduct and Ethics program is led by the Vice President for Business Conduct and Ethics, who reports to the Senior Vice President, Chief Global Affairs & Legal Officer [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_106]. The program includes a review process for allegations—investigations are reported to the Board’s Audit Committee—and an ethics line available in 65 countries and 165 languages [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_106]. Employees are prohibited from bribing anyone, whether in dealings with governments or the private sector [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_107]. Third-party due diligence is conducted on a risk-based approach before entering business relationships, and employees must disclose and seek approval for qualifying gifts or services received from third parties or given to government officials [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_107]. Amazon participates in the OECD’s Anti-Corruption Leaders Hub (ACLH), a public-private working group focused on digitizing compliance information and expanding local partner vetting programs [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_107].

### Climate-Related and Human Rights Governance  
Climate-related governance is overseen by the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee, which receives regular updates from the Chief Sustainability Officer [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_103][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104]. The Sustainability team maintains a companywide carbon system of record to track emissions at the business level and reports quarterly to senior leadership on environmental and sustainability performance [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104]. Human rights governance includes oversight by the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee for policies on human rights and ethical business practices, and by the Leadership Development and Compensation Committee for internal human capital management—including nondiscrimination, workplace safety, and culture [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104]. Amazon employs a Human Rights Officer (HRO) who reports directly to the Chief Sustainability Officer and facilitates regular risk management updates to senior leadership [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104].

### Shareholder Engagement and Ethics Training  
Amazon conducts year-round engagement with shareholders through a dedicated team whose full-time responsibilities include communicating with investors, management, and Board members [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104]. In 2025, shareholder feedback informed Board discussions on sustainability, corporate governance, and executive compensation—including the advisory vote approving named executive officer compensation [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_103]. All employees receive Code of Conduct training during onboarding and periodic refreshers; Board members and leaders receive specific training on the Code of Conduct, anti-corruption, and competition [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_107].

### Board Oversight and Committee Structure  
Amazon’s Board of Directors is responsible for the control and direction of the company and represents shareholders with the primary purpose of building long-term shareholder value [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_101]. In 2025, the Board held six in-person meetings and participated in regularly scheduled teleconference discussions [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_101]. Risk oversight is delegated to four standing committees: the Audit Committee (six meetings), Leadership Development and Compensation Committee (five meetings), Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee (four meetings), and Security Committee (two meetings) [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_102]. The Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee oversees risks related to sustainability, environmental and corporate social responsibility practices, operations and supply chain, and responsible AI development and AI governance [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_102][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_103][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104]. The Chief Sustainability Officer provides regular updates to this committee on sustainability performance and human rights matters [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_103][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104].

### Anti-Corruption Governance and Controls  
Amazon’s Business Conduct and Ethics program is led by the Vice President for Business Conduct and Ethics, who reports to the Senior Vice President, Chief Global Affairs & Legal Officer [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_106]. The program includes a review process for allegations—investigations are reported to the Board’s Audit Committee—and an ethics line available in 65 countries and 165 languages [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_106]. Employees are prohibited from bribing anyone, whether in dealings with governments or the private sector [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_107]. Third-party due diligence is conducted on a risk-based approach before entering business relationships, and employees must disclose and seek approval for qualifying gifts or services received from third parties or given to government officials [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_107]. Amazon participates in the OECD’s Anti-Corruption Leaders Hub (ACLH), a public-private working group focused on digitizing compliance information and expanding local partner vetting programs [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_107].

### Climate-Related and Human Rights Governance  
Climate-related governance is overseen by the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee, which receives regular updates from the Chief Sustainability Officer [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_103][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104]. The Sustainability team maintains a companywide carbon system of record to track emissions at the business level and reports quarterly to senior leadership on environmental and sustainability performance [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104]. Human rights governance includes oversight by the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee for policies on human rights and ethical business practices, and by the Leadership Development and Compensation Committee for internal human capital management—including nondiscrimination, workplace safety, and culture [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104]. Amazon employs a Human Rights Officer (HRO) who reports directly to the Chief Sustainability Officer and facilitates regular risk management updates to senior leadership [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104].

### Shareholder Engagement and Ethics Training  
Amazon conducts year-round engagement with shareholders through a dedicated team whose full-time responsibilities include communicating with investors, management, and Board members [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104]. In 2025, shareholder feedback informed Board discussions on sustainability, corporate governance, and executive compensation—including the advisory vote approving named executive officer compensation [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_103]. All employees receive Code of Conduct training during onboarding and periodic refreshers; Board members and leaders receive specific training on the Code of Conduct, anti-corruption, and competition [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_107].

### Not covered in source material  
The context does not provide: (1) board diversity metrics (e.g., gender, ethnicity, tenure) required under GRI 2-13; (2) quantified anti-corruption KPIs such as substantiated bribery cases, average resolution time, or root-cause trends per GRI 205-2; (3) forward-looking, time-bound targets for board climate competency; (4) anti-corruption program maturity targets aligned with GRI 205-3; (5) methodology or frequency of full Board-level climate risk challenge sessions per TCFD Governance A1.1; (6) baseline and 2025 values for ethics line report volumes or whistleblower case resolution times; (7) audit committee oversight of climate-related financial risks per TCFD.

### GRI 302 Energy  
Amazon reported 131,000 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of carbon-free energy production annually in 2025 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_22]. Carbon-free energy includes electricity from wind, solar, nuclear, hydroelectric, and geothermal sources, as well as site energy contracts and green tariffs that add new renewable projects to the grid [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_14]. This volume reflects Amazon’s global portfolio of 375 utility-scale projects (264 solar, 109 wind, two nuclear) and 337 rooftop solar installations [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_22]. AWS aims to procure renewable electricity in the same grids where it consumes electricity; when not feasible, it may procure renewable energy attributes elsewhere [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_113]. Emissions from purchased electricity (Scope 2) totaled 3.74 million metric tons of CO₂e (MMT CO₂e) in 2025—up 34% from 2.80 MMT CO₂e in 2024—driven by data center expansion, delivery network electrification, and building electrification [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_112][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_19].

### GRI 303 Water  
Amazon achieved 75% progress toward its goal of becoming water positive—returning more water to communities than it uses—across global direct data center operations by 2030 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33]. In 2025, its leased, owned, and shared data centers withdrew 9.4 billion liters of water [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33]. Of this, 48% occurred in low water stress regions and 22% in high or extremely high water stress regions, per WRI’s Aqueduct Water Risk Atlas [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_34]. Progress is measured using the Water Positive Methodology: (reused water + replenishment volume) ÷ (total water withdrawal − water from sustainable sources) × 100% [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_16]. By end-2025, Amazon had invested in 45 water replenishment projects globally, returning 9.4 billion liters to communities and contracting for over 18 billion liters of annual replenishment volume in future years [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_37]. In India—where Amazon achieved 120% water positivity in 2025, two years ahead of its 2027 target—on-site sewage treatment plants at 28 buildings provided an estimated 298 million liters of recycled water annually, and rainwater harvesting pits collected ~178 million liters for groundwater recharge [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_37].

### GRI 305 Emissions  
Amazon’s total carbon footprint (Scopes 1, 2, and 3) was 80.85 million metric tons of CO₂e (MMT CO₂e) in 2025, up 16% from 69.55 MMT CO₂e in 2024 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_113][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_5]. Scope 1 emissions were 15.37 MMT CO₂e, Scope 2 emissions were 3.74 MMT CO₂e, and Scope 3 emissions were 61.74 MMT CO₂e [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_112]. Environmental Attribute Certificates (EACs) delivered a net reduction of 199.4 thousand metric tons of CO₂e (K MTCO₂e) across Scopes 1, 3.1, 3.3, and 3.4—including 41.2 K MTCO₂e reduction in Scope 1 via Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) and Renewable Diesel certificates [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_15][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_113]. Carbon intensity was 112.8 gCO₂e/$Revenue in 2025 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_112][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_5].

### GRI 306 Waste  
In 2025, Amazon diverted 84% of its operational waste from landfill and incineration without energy recovery—including 82% through recycling or composting and 2% through incineration with energy recovery [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_47]. Waste per shipped unit decreased by 5% compared to 2024 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_47][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_41]. Cardboard and wood constituted 64% of Amazon’s operational waste footprint, with nearly 100% recycled [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_47]. Amazon reused or donated 343,000 assets and materials in 2025 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_45], avoided over one million hard drive purchases since 2023 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_41], and prevented 225,000 metric tons of CO₂e through reuse and resale of data center hardware since 2020 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_45].

### TCFD Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics & Targets  
Amazon’s climate strategy is anchored in The Climate Pledge and structured around five pillars: reducing supply chain emissions, decarbonizing direct operations, addressing Scope 2 emissions, scaling carbon neutralization, and driving collective action [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_10]. Risk management integrates AI tools to identify high-risk suppliers and prioritize audits [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_10][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_13]. Key metrics include carbon intensity (gCO₂e/$Revenue), water use effectiveness (0.12 L/kWh in 2025), and waste diversion rate (84%) [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_112][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_35][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_47]. Targets include net-zero emissions by 2040, water positivity in data centers by 2030, and 100,000 electric delivery vans by 2030 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_5][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33].

### Not covered in source material  
The context does not specify location-based versus market-based Scope 2 emissions separately, nor does it define the accounting methodology used. It omits the baseline year for The Climate Pledge’s net-zero target and provides no SBTi-aligned interim emissions reduction target. Absolute emissions for Scope 3 subcategories beyond those listed in the 2019–2025 table (e.g., 3.5, 3.11) are not disclosed for 2025. No quantitative data is provided on total waste generation volumes (e.g., metric tons), only diversion rates and intensity metrics. The context also lacks explanation of operational barriers limiting Scope 1 reductions—e.g., physical constraints on SAF availability despite certificate purchases [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_11].

### GRI 302 Energy  
Amazon reported 131,000 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of carbon-free energy production annually in 2025 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_22]. Carbon-free energy includes electricity from wind, solar, nuclear, hydroelectric, and geothermal sources, as well as site energy contracts and green tariffs that add new renewable projects to the grid [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_14]. AWS aims to procure renewable electricity in the same grids where it consumes electricity; when not feasible, it may procure renewable energy attributes in other locations [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_113]. In 2025, Amazon’s emissions from purchased electricity (Scope 2) totaled 3.74 million metric tons of CO₂e (MMT CO₂e), representing a 34% increase from 2024 and 5% of its total carbon footprint [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_19][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_112]. This growth was driven by electricity use in data centers, electrification of the delivery network, and building electrification [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_19]. Amazon’s global data center portfolio achieved a Water Use Effectiveness (WUE) of 0.12 liters per kilowatt-hour (L/kWh) in 2025—a 20% improvement from 2024 and 52% since 2021—reflecting enhanced energy-water efficiency linkages [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_35].

### GRI 303 Water  
Amazon achieved 75% progress toward its goal of becoming water positive—returning more water to communities than it uses—across global direct data center operations by 2030 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33]. In 2025, Amazon’s global leased, owned, and shared data centers withdrew 9.4 billion liters of water [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33]. Of this, 48% occurred in low water stress regions and 22% in high or extremely high water stress regions, per WRI’s Aqueduct Water Risk Atlas [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_34]. Amazon measured progress using its Water Positive Methodology, which calculates the ratio of reused water plus replenishment volume to total water withdrawal minus water from sustainable sources, multiplied by 100% [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_16]. By end-2025, Amazon had invested in 45 water replenishment projects globally, returning 9.4 billion liters of water to communities and contracting for over 18 billion liters of annual replenishment volume in future years [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_37]. In India—where Amazon achieved 120% water positivity in 2025, two years ahead of its 2027 target—on-site sewage treatment plants at 28 buildings provided an estimated 298 million liters of recycled water annually, and rainwater harvesting pits collected ~178 million liters for groundwater recharge [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_37].

### GRI 305 Emissions  
Amazon’s total carbon footprint (Scopes 1, 2, and 3) was 80.85 MMT CO₂e in 2025, up 16% from 69.55 MMT CO₂e in 2024 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_113][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_5]. Scope 1 emissions were 15.37 MMT CO₂e, Scope 2 emissions were 3.74 MMT CO₂e, and Scope 3 emissions were 61.74 MMT CO₂e [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_112]. Environmental Attribute Certificates (EACs) delivered a net reduction of 199.4 thousand metric tons of CO₂e (K MTCO₂e) across Scopes 1, 3.1, 3.3, and 3.4—including 41.2 K MTCO₂e reduction in Scope 1 via Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) and Renewable Diesel certificates [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_15][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_113]. Carbon intensity—measured as grams of CO₂e per dollar of revenue—was 112.8 gCO₂e/$Revenue in 2025 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_112][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_5]. Amazon’s Climate Pledge commits to net-zero carbon emissions across global operations by 2040 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_10].

### GRI 306 Waste  
In 2025, Amazon diverted 84% of its operational waste from landfill and incineration without energy recovery—including 82% through recycling or composting and 2% through incineration with energy recovery [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_47]. Waste per shipped unit decreased by 5% compared to 2024 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_47][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_41]. Cardboard and wood constituted 64% of Amazon’s operational waste footprint, with nearly 100% recycled [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_47]. Amazon reused or donated 343,000 assets and materials in 2025 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_45], avoided over one million hard drive purchases since 2023 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_41], and prevented 225,000 metric tons of CO₂e through reuse and resale of data center hardware since 2020 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_45].

### TCFD Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics & Targets  
Amazon’s climate strategy is anchored in The Climate Pledge and structured around five pillars: reducing supply chain emissions, decarbonizing direct operations, addressing Scope 2 emissions, scaling carbon neutralization, and driving collective action [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_10]. Risk management integrates AI tools to identify high-risk suppliers and prioritize audits [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_10][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_13]. Key metrics include carbon intensity (gCO₂e/$Revenue), water use effectiveness (L/kWh), and waste diversion rate (%), with targets including net-zero by 2040, water positivity in data centers by 2030, and 100,000 electric delivery vans by 2030 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_5][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_33].

### Not covered in source material  
The context does not specify whether Amazon reports location-based versus market-based Scope 2 emissions separately, nor does it disclose absolute Scope 3 subcategory totals beyond those listed in the 2019–2025 carbon footprint table (e.g., full breakdowns for all Scope 3 categories through 2025). It also lacks explicit disclosure on methane or other short-lived climate pollutant inventories outside of super pollutant abatement initiatives, and no quantitative data is provided on waste generation volumes (e.g., total tons of waste generated) — only diversion rates and intensity metrics.

### GRI 403 Occupational Health & Safety  
Amazon’s global operations safety performance improved in 2025, with a 14% year-over-year reduction in the Global Recordable Incident Rate (RIR) — defined as work-related injuries requiring more than basic first-aid treatment — and a 14% reduction in the Global Lost Time Incident Rate (LTIR) — defined as injuries resulting in time away from work [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_76][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_78]. Over six years, the global RIR improved by 43% and the global LTIR by 70% [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_76][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_78]. In the U.S., under General Warehousing and Storage, the RIR improved 16% year over year; the LTIR was flat year over year but improved 79% over six years [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_76]. Under Courier and Express Delivery Services, the RIR improved 19% year over year and the LTIR improved 28% year over year [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_76]. Amazon conducted 10.4 million safety inspections globally in 2025 — a 33% increase from 2024 — to validate engineering controls [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_77]. The company employs over 11,000 safety professionals worldwide [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_76].

### GRI 404 Training  
Amazon invested over $2.5 billion in safety efforts since 2019, including training programs grounded in prevention-through-design principles [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_78]. In 2025, 599,000 U.S. employees participated in upskilling programs since the 2019 Upskilling Pledge launch [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_69]. The U.S. Mechatronics and Robotics Apprenticeship — a Department of Labor–registered program — achieved 100% employment placement for graduates in 2025, with average annual earnings $10,000 higher than typical entry-level fulfillment-center wages [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_70]. Over 16,400 U.S. employees completed English-language proficiency programs in 2025 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_69]. Amazon delivered 52 new e-learning resources and updated 90 existing modules for human rights–related training, including a three-day immersive program for employees in human rights roles [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_63]. For suppliers, Amazon deployed online trainings for 1,600 suppliers on Supply Chain Standards and provided access to 90 third-party online trainings across 12 human rights topics [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_84].

### GRI 405 Diversity  
Amazon’s 2025 pay equity review found women globally earned 100.0% of what men earned in comparable jobs, and women in the U.S. earned 99.9 cents per dollar earned by men in comparable roles [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_71][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_70]. Racial and ethnic minorities in the U.S. earned 99.0 cents per dollar earned by white employees in comparable jobs [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_71][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_70]. “Together at Amazon” reached over 647,000 corporate and operations employees in 2025, including participation across 2,300 Employee-Led Groups (ELGs) spanning multiple countries and regions [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_75]. Amazon advanced military inclusion via the Duty to Data Center program and introduced a Military Spouse Deployment Benefit [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_75].

### GRI 414 Supplier Social Assessment  
Amazon requires suppliers to comply with its Supply Chain Standards — available in 23 languages — and mandates that suppliers hold their own subcontractors and labor agents to applicable laws and these standards [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_84][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_83]. In 2025, Amazon hosted 29 in-person human rights workshops across 13 countries, engaging 650 participants from 480 suppliers; 60% of suppliers attending workshops between 2023 and 2025 reduced high-risk findings [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_84]. The company redesigned its Human Rights and Environmental Complaints Form — available in 19 languages — and addressed 100% of the 850 complaints submitted in 2025 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_66].

### TCFD Strategy (social impacts of climate transition)  
Amazon aims to integrate human rights due diligence into its decarbonization efforts to identify how its shift to a green economy affects communities in its value chain [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_66]. In 2025, the company focused on carbon-free energy procurement, climate finance, and community-based carbon neutralization projects to align its net-zero carbon commitment with human rights principles [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_66][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_67].

### GRI 403 Occupational Health & Safety  
Amazon’s global operations safety performance demonstrated year-over-year improvement in 2025, with a 14% reduction in the Global Recordable Incident Rate (RIR) — defined as work-related injuries requiring more than basic first-aid treatment — and a 14% reduction in the Global Lost Time Incident Rate (LTIR) — defined as injuries resulting in time away from work [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_76][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_78]. Over six years, the global RIR improved by 43% and the global LTIR by 70% [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_76][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_78]. In the U.S., under the General Warehousing and Storage classification, the RIR improved 16% year over year and 39% over six years; the LTIR was flat year over year but improved 79% over six years [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_76]. Under Courier and Express Delivery Services, the RIR improved 19% year over year and 59% over six years, while the LTIR improved 28% year over year and 81% over six years [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_76]. Amazon conducted 10.4 million safety inspections globally in 2025 — a 33% increase from 2024 — to validate engineering controls and inform iterative improvements [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_77]. The company employs over 11,000 safety professionals worldwide [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_76]. *However, the report does not disclose the percentage of employees covered by occupational health services, frequency of mandatory health assessments, or baseline-aligned science-based safety targets (e.g., RIR target for 2030), as required by GRI 403-3 and TCFD-aligned goal-setting expectations.*

### GRI 404 Training  
Amazon invested over $2.5 billion in safety efforts since 2019, including training programs grounded in prevention-through-design principles [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_78]. In 2025, 599,000 U.S. employees participated in upskilling programs since the 2019 Upskilling Pledge launch [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_69]. The U.S. Mechatronics and Robotics Apprenticeship — a Department of Labor–registered program — achieved 100% employment placement for graduates in 2025, with average annual earnings $10,000 higher than typical entry-level fulfillment-center wages [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_70]. Over 16,400 U.S. employees completed English-language proficiency programs in 2025 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_69]. Amazon also delivered 52 new e-learning resources and updated 90 existing modules for human rights–related training, including a three-day immersive program for employees in human rights roles [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_63]. For suppliers, Amazon deployed online trainings for 1,600 suppliers on Supply Chain Standards and provided access to 90 third-party online trainings across 12 human rights topics [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_84]. *The report does not disclose average annual training hours per employee, nor disaggregation by gender, job level, or geography, as required by GRI 404-3.*

### GRI 405 Diversity  
Amazon’s 2025 pay equity review found women globally earned 100.0% of what men earned in comparable jobs, and women in the U.S. earned 99.9 cents per dollar earned by men in comparable roles [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_71][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_70]. Racial and ethnic minorities in the U.S. earned 99.0 cents per dollar earned by white employees in comparable jobs [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_71][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_70]. “Together at Amazon” reached over 647,000 corporate and operations employees in 2025, including participation across 2,300 Employee-Led Groups (ELGs) spanning multiple countries and regions [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_75]. Amazon advanced military inclusion via the Duty to Data Center program and introduced a Military Spouse Deployment Benefit [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_75]. *However, the report does not disclose representation of women or racial/ethnic minorities in senior management or executive leadership roles, as required by GRI 405-2.*

### GRI 414 Supplier Social Assessment  
Amazon requires suppliers to comply with its Supply Chain Standards — available in 23 languages — and mandates that suppliers hold their own subcontractors and labor agents to applicable laws and these standards [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_84][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_83]. In 2025, Amazon hosted 29 in-person human rights workshops across 13 countries, engaging 650 participants from 480 suppliers; 60% of suppliers attending workshops between 2023 and 2025 reduced high-risk findings [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_84]. The company redesigned its Human Rights and Environmental Complaints Form — available in 19 languages — and addressed 100% of the 850 complaints submitted in 2025 [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_66]. *The report does not disclose the percentage of Tier 1 suppliers assessed, non-compliance resolution timelines, or methodology for assessing tier-2+ suppliers, as required by GRI 414-3.*

### TCFD Strategy (social impacts of climate transition)  
Amazon aims to integrate human rights due diligence into its decarbonization efforts to identify how its shift to a green economy affects communities in its value chain [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_66]. In 2025, the company focused on carbon-free energy procurement, climate finance, and community-based carbon neutralization projects to align its net-zero carbon commitment with human rights principles [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_66][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_67]. *The report does not conduct or disclose a TCFD-aligned social risk scenario analysis covering workforce displacement, reskilling needs, or community-level just transition impacts of decarbonization.*

### Not covered in source material  
GRI 403-3 (occupational health service coverage and health assessment frequency); GRI 404-3 (average annual training hours per employee, disaggregated by gender, level, geography); GRI 405-2 (senior management diversity representation); GRI 414-3 (Tier 1 supplier assessment rate, tier-2+ methodology); TCFD-aligned social risk scenario analysis; science-based occupational safety targets (e.g., RIR <1.0 by 2030); time-bound, quantified targets for reducing supplier high-risk findings.

### Board Oversight and Committee Structure  
Amazon’s Board of Directors is responsible for the control and direction of the company and represents shareholders with the primary purpose of building long-term shareholder value [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_101]. In 2025, the Board held six in-person meetings and participated in regularly scheduled teleconference discussions [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_101]. Risk oversight is delegated to four standing committees: the Audit Committee (six meetings), Leadership Development and Compensation Committee (five meetings), Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee (four meetings), and Security Committee (two meetings) [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_102]. The Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee oversees risks related to sustainability, environmental and corporate social responsibility practices, operations and supply chain, and responsible AI development and AI governance [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_102][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_103][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104]. The Chief Sustainability Officer provides regular updates to this committee on sustainability performance and human rights matters [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_103][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104].

### Anti-Corruption Governance and Controls  
Amazon’s Business Conduct and Ethics program is led by the Vice President for Business Conduct and Ethics, who reports to the Senior Vice President, Chief Global Affairs & Legal Officer [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_106]. The program includes a review process for allegations—investigations are reported to the Board’s Audit Committee—and an ethics line available in 65 countries and 165 languages [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_106]. Employees are prohibited from bribing anyone, whether in dealings with governments or the private sector [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_107]. Third-party due diligence is conducted on a risk-based approach before entering business relationships, and employees must disclose and seek approval for qualifying gifts or services received from third parties or given to government officials [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_107]. Amazon participates in the OECD’s Anti-Corruption Leaders Hub (ACLH), a public-private working group focused on digitizing compliance information and expanding local partner vetting programs [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_107].

### Climate-Related and Human Rights Governance  
Climate-related governance is overseen by the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee, which receives regular updates from the Chief Sustainability Officer [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_103][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104]. The Sustainability team maintains a companywide carbon system of record to track emissions at the business level and reports quarterly to senior leadership on environmental and sustainability performance [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104]. Human rights governance includes oversight by the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee for policies on human rights and ethical business practices, and by the Leadership Development and Compensation Committee for internal human capital management—including nondiscrimination, workplace safety, and culture [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104]. Amazon employs a Human Rights Officer (HRO) who reports directly to the Chief Sustainability Officer and facilitates regular risk management updates to senior leadership [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104].

### Shareholder Engagement and Ethics Training  
Amazon conducts year-round engagement with shareholders through a dedicated team whose full-time responsibilities include communicating with investors, management, and Board members [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104]. In 2025, shareholder feedback informed Board discussions on sustainability, corporate governance, and executive compensation—including the advisory vote approving named executive officer compensation [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_103]. All employees receive Code of Conduct training during onboarding and periodic refreshers; Board members and leaders receive specific training on the Code of Conduct, anti-corruption, and competition [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_107].

### Not covered in source material  
The context does not provide: (1) board composition data by gender, ethnicity, or tenure required under GRI 2-13; (2) substantiated bribery allegations, investigation outcomes, or average resolution time per GRI 205-2; (3) frequency, methodology, or documented outcomes of full Board-level climate risk challenge sessions per TCFD Governance A1.1; (4) audit committee oversight of climate-related financial risks (e.g., stranded assets, transition cost accounting); (5) baseline or 2025 values for ethics line report volumes, whistleblower case resolution times, or substantiated corruption incidents; (6) forward-looking targets for board climate competency (e.g., % of directors completing climate risk training by 2027) or anti-corruption program maturity (e.g., % of high-risk third parties subject to enhanced due diligence by 2026); (7) quantified coverage or depth metrics for third-party anti-corruption due diligence (e.g., % of Tier 1 suppliers assessed annually). These disclosures are absent from the provided context and therefore cannot be reported.

### Board Oversight and Committee Structure  
Amazon’s Board of Directors is responsible for the control and direction of the company and represents shareholders with the primary purpose of building long-term shareholder value [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_101]. In 2025, the Board held six in-person meetings and participated in regularly scheduled teleconference discussions [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_101]. Risk oversight is delegated to four standing committees: the Audit Committee (six meetings), Leadership Development and Compensation Committee (five meetings), Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee (four meetings), and Security Committee (two meetings) [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_102]. The Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee oversees risks related to sustainability, environmental and corporate social responsibility practices, operations and supply chain, and responsible AI development and AI governance [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_102][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_103][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104]. The Chief Sustainability Officer provides regular updates to this committee on sustainability performance and human rights matters [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_103][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104].

### Anti-Corruption Governance and Controls  
Amazon’s Business Conduct and Ethics program is led by the Vice President for Business Conduct and Ethics, who reports to the Senior Vice President, Chief Global Affairs & Legal Officer [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_106]. The program includes a review process for allegations—investigations are reported to the Board’s Audit Committee—and an ethics line available in 65 countries and 165 languages [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_106]. Employees are prohibited from bribing anyone, whether in dealings with governments or the private sector [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_107]. Third-party due diligence is conducted on a risk-based approach before entering business relationships, and employees must disclose and seek approval for qualifying gifts or services received from third parties or given to government officials [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_107]. Amazon participates in the OECD’s Anti-Corruption Leaders Hub (ACLH), a public-private working group focused on digitizing compliance information and expanding local partner vetting programs [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_107].

### Climate-Related and Human Rights Governance  
Climate-related governance is overseen by the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee, which receives regular updates from the Chief Sustainability Officer [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_103][2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104]. The Sustainability team maintains a companywide carbon system of record to track emissions at the business level and reports quarterly to senior leadership on environmental and sustainability performance [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104]. Human rights governance includes oversight by the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee for policies on human rights and ethical business practices, and by the Leadership Development and Compensation Committee for internal human capital management—including nondiscrimination, workplace safety, and culture [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104]. Amazon employs a Human Rights Officer (HRO) who reports directly to the Chief Sustainability Officer and facilitates regular risk management updates to senior leadership [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104].

### Shareholder Engagement and Ethics Training  
Amazon conducts year-round engagement with shareholders through a dedicated team whose full-time responsibilities include communicating with investors, management, and Board members [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_104]. In 2025, shareholder feedback informed Board discussions on sustainability, corporate governance, and executive compensation—including the advisory vote approving named executive officer compensation [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_103]. All employees receive Code of Conduct training during onboarding and periodic refreshers; Board members and leaders receive specific training on the Code of Conduct, anti-corruption, and competition [2025-amazon-sustainability-report_chunk_107].

The context does not provide: (1) board composition data by gender, ethnicity, or tenure required under GRI 2-13; (2) substantiated bribery allegations, investigation outcomes, or average resolution time per GRI 205-2; (3) frequency, methodology, or documented outcomes of full Board-level climate risk challenge sessions per TCFD Governance A1.1; (4) audit committee oversight of climate-related financial risks (e.g., stranded assets, transition cost accounting); (5) baseline or 2025 values for ethics line report volumes, whistleblower case resolution times, or substantiated corruption incidents; (6) forward-looking targets for board climate competency (e.g., % of directors completing climate risk training by 2027) or anti-corruption program maturity (e.g., % of high-risk third parties subject to enhanced due diligence by 2026); (7) quantified coverage or depth metrics for third-party anti-corruption due diligence (e.g., % of Tier 1 suppliers assessed annually).
